# Restrict access to content

![Avatar](https://support.khanacademy.org/system/photos/360515768452/profile_image_396036849511_526991.png)

Is there a way to restrict student access to content?  I understand we do not want to discourage learning of any kind, but I want to help focus students on assignments.  I have students who are not doing the assigned work and are instead completing other Kahn (unassigned) work.  It'd be a helpful option to have students only have access to assigned work, if they need this as a modification, to help them focus.

### Didn't find what you were looking for?

![Avatar](https://support.khanacademy.org/system/photos/361060249891/profile_image_396542298452_526991.png)

Hi Kris,

My name is Carol and I'm from the Khan Academy Support Team!

Our approach is an open education for everyone, so we strive to make our content accessible to anyone seeking it on the website, thus, we do not currently offer any form of parental control or content restrictions on Khan Academy.

I completely understand and appreciate your concerns about your students accessing content that's appropriate for them. Please know we welcome your feedback, and we also understand that no curriculum will work for everyone and that you’ll want to follow your judgment as a parent and/or teacher regarding what content your child should have access to and how they use Khan Academy.

Additionally, for an explanation of Khan Academy's Content Principles, please check out [this article.](/hc/en-us/articles/360054562832-What-are-Khan-Academy-s-Content-Principles-)

![Avatar](https://support.khanacademy.org/system/photos/360990418011/profile_image_8530959907_526991.png)

Hi Kris,

Unfortunately, it is not possible to restrict access to content. If your students are working on content that you've specifically assigned, I suggest continuing to remind them to go back to their assignments list as soon as they complete an assignment.

Alternatively, if you use Google Classroom, you may find it useful to post the assignments there as well, which may help students stay focused on what they need to do. However, please note that you will still need to assign the content on Khan Academy in order to be able to view their assignment scores.

I hope this helps! Please let me know if you have any additional questions!

# How do I access parental controls?

Khan Academy Kids provides parental controls to focus a child's learning experience in the app. If parents wish to limit access to certain sections of the app (such as videos or seasonal themes) these preferences can be configured in the app’s Parent Section.

Please note that these preferences are only available in the parent (not teacher) version of the app at this time, and you must be using the latest version of the app in order to access them.

Welcome to Khan Academy! Parents are key in supporting their children’s learning on Khan Academy. We are here to get you and your kiddos started as quickly and easily as possible.

We have split this guide into different sections. You can complete Steps 1-4 in about 15 minutes, but you can skip ahead to just the parts you need using the links in the steps below:

**Step 1:** [Create or log into your existing Khan Academy parent account](#h.3ftj59fbzkdo)

**Step 2:** [View your Parent Dashboard](#h.d4gec0l5cf91)

**Step 3:** [Connect your children to your parent account](#h_01JP64SBSDZX1WCHYV13R6CEDG)

**Step 4:** [Have your child log in](#h.bb4d5p3xisnf)

**Step 5:** [Learn more about and get started with Course Mastery](#h.t6ezg4iy6gcf)

**Step 6**: [Following your child's progress](#h_01JP65SKVCA3FQBTPZRB5ET6S1)

**Step 7**: [Consider Khanmigo](#01JSHPPWT4AWBFMYHZ7KXDEJE2)

-----

## **Step 1: Create or log into your Khan Academy parent account**

First things first: if you don’t already have one, you’ll want to create an account for yourself. To do this, go to the [Khan Academy home page](https://www.khanacademy.org/) and click "Log in" or "Sign up" 

## **Step 2: View your Parent Dashboard**

Once you're logged in, you'll see Parent Dashboard. This is your hub for all things Khan Academy for Parents.  

You can always come back to the Parent Dashboard by clicking your name in the top righthand corner, and "Parent Dashboard" from the dropdown.

If you do not see the Parent Dashboard option in the drop-down menu, double check you have selected the Parent role on your account settings page.

## **Step 3: Connect your children to your Parent Account**

To connect with your child, click on the **Add a child** button on the Parent Dashboard**.**

If your child does not have a Khan Academy account:

* If your child is under 13, you can create an account for them by choosing a username + password they can use to log in.
* If they are above 13, you can send an invitation to their email address to sign up for an account on their own. Then they can invite you to connect you as their parent from their Learner Home.

If your child already has a Khan Academy account: 

* If your child is over 13 and already has an email on their account, you can simply send a parent invitation to that email. They’ll need to log in and accept the invitation from their Learner Home.  
    
  However, if your child is over 13 and their account doesn't have an email address yet, they’ll need to add one first. After that, you’ll be able to send the parent invitation normally.

* If your child is under 13 and has a Khan Academy account without an email address, they will need to log in to their account and invite you as their parent on their Settings page.

* If your child is over 13 and has an account without an email, they'll first need to add an email to their account so you, as a parent, can send the invite.

## **Step 4: Helping your child log In**

Now that you’re connected to your child’s account, the next step is to have your child log into their account. Your child can then log in using the username and password you created for them, or through their existing login methods on their account. 

Need help? Check out this article: [How do I reset my child's password?](https://support.khanacademy.org/hc/en-us/articles/202260314-How-do-I-reset-my-child-s-password)

## **Step 5: Your child starts working on Khan Academy!**

Khan Academy offers a variety of material about a wide variety of subjects in [50+ languages!](https://support.khanacademy.org/hc/en-us/articles/226457308-What-languages-is-Khan-Academy-available-in) We have articles, videos, exercises, quizzes, unit tests, and more that your child can learn with. All content is completely free too!

* Topics include science, English Language Arts, math, grammar, art history, computer programming, economics, AP prep, SAT prep, and more!
* For state-aligned math content, [check out our standards mapping by state](https://www.khanacademy.org/regions/united-states).
* You and your child can view all our courses by clicking the **Explore**dropdown menu in the top left corner of any page, or searching for a specific topic.

Your child can work independently, or via assignments you create for them on the Assignments tab of your Parent Dashboard. 

## **Step 6: Following your child’s progress**

You can view your child’s progress on Khan Academy in 3 places:

**1. The Activity Overview Report on the Activity tab**  
Click on your child’s name to view their activity in the courses across Khan Academy.  This includes work your child did at home and at school, broken down by Khan Academy course. 

**2. The Individual Student Report from the Activity tab**  
Click the person icon![](/hc/article_attachments/34987493495437)next to you child's name to be taken directly to their Learner Home. Here you'll see additional progress info, and if applicable, their Khanmigo Chat History and Khanmigo settings page. 

![](/hc/article_attachments/34987482935821)**3. The Assignment Scores report from the Assignments tab**  
If you have made assignments for your child, you can see the scores for them here.

## **Step 7: Consider Khanmigo!**

Khanmigo is our AI-powered tutor for learners, and also has a variety of tools built just for parents! Khanmigo is a great option if your child could use an additional helping hand while working on Khan Academy, and if you would like some additional tools in your toolkit when helping them do so.

You can learn more about Khanmigo for learners and parents here [on the Khanmigo website](https://www.khanmigo.ai/learners) and on the [Khanmigo section of the Help Center.](https://support.khanacademy.org/hc/en-us/categories/24449383583757-Khanmigo)   
![](/hc/article_attachments/36064835279117)

---

This guide covers the essentials, and for a complete, in-depth walkthrough, consider our [*Khan for Families*](https://www.khanacademy.org/khan-for-parents/khan-for-families) course

We hope this helped get you started as a parent on Khan Academy! If you have any questions or need assistance, feel free to [reach out to the Khan Academy Support Team!](https://support.khanacademy.org/hc/en-us/requests/new)We are here and happy to help.

# What is Khan Academy?

## What parents need to know

Khan Academy is an educational platform. It helps students learn about a range of topics using video lessons and quizzes.

![Khan Academy logo](https://www.internetmatters.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Khan-Academy-feature-300x158.webp)

## In this guide

## What is Khan Academy?

Khan Academy is an online learning resource that lets users learn about various topics by watching short videos and completing quizzes, which the user can do at their own pace. Khan Academy offers subjects like Maths, Computing, and Science..

The Khan Academy app is available on Android and iOS and is also available through internet browsers. All courses and lessons at Khan Academy are free. An app designed specifically for children aged 2-8 also exists called [Khan Academy Kids](https://learn.khanacademy.org/khan-academy-kids/).

## How it works

To start using Khan Academy, you must sign up and select a course that you’d like to take. Once you enroll in your course, you will get access to video lessons and quizzes. The platform organises these into groups called units.

These units are sequential, meaning that as you complete each unit, you will learn enough to be able to understand the next unit. However, if you already know the information in a particular unit, you can skip ahead to the next one without having to complete the ones preceding it.

Khan Academy has a gamified approach to learning, [similar to other skill-building apps like Duolingo](/advice/apps-and-platforms/skills-building/duolingo/), with users receiving points and badges for watching videos and completing quizzes. Receiving points can allow users to ‘evolve’ their Khan Academy avatar, getting a different version of their profile’s avatar. This can motivate children to stick with Khan Academy and complete lessons regularly.

Khan Academy has a community forum, where users can ask each other questions and get advice on the subjects they are studying. This forum is based heavily around education and the Khan Academy platform. Because of this, it is unlikely that users will be exposed to any inappropriate or upsetting content while using it.

There is a range of educational subjects that can be studied, such as Maths, Science and Economics, but Khan Academy also offers Life skills courses. These units include lessons on Internet Safety, Financial and Social Media Literacy, and how AI can be used in education. These options make Khan Academy a beneficial app for children even if they don’t use it for school subjects.

![A few people holding their devices with a logo inside it representing Internet Matters' artificial intelligence assistant. Text reads: Ask Internet Matters](https://www.internetmatters.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/hero-ask-internet-matters-300x158.webp)

### Need a quick answer?

Ask our AI assistant about devices, apps and games.

## Khan Academy parental controls

Khan Academy is an educational platform, with content that is appropriate for all ages. However, there is still an option to create a parent account and monitor your child’s activity.

To do this, parents must create a parent account and then send an invite to their child’s account. Once the child accepts the invitation, the parent will be able to view their activity on Khan Academy. However, this is purely a monitoring role, as parents cannot set any controls on their child’s account.

Being able to monitor activity will let parents stay aware of how much studying their child is doing, and it also lets them know what courses they are undertaking. With Khan Academy having lessons intended for all ages, from primary school to university students, this feature will mean parents are aware if their 8-year-old child is mistakenly signed up to a university economics course.

If you have a child younger than 8-years-old, you can create an account for them on Khan Academy Kids rather than regular Khan Academy. This app only has content meant for children and is more engaging for younger audiences. Animal characters guide children, and lessons use interactive activities like games and books. Using this app will also mean your child can’t access the community features of Khan Academy.

The Kid’s app does include parental controls. Because the app targets children, developers did not need to add many controls. The only settings parents can change are visual ones such as having seasonal themes.

![Digital Matters logo on white background.](https://www.internetmatters.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/digital-matters-logo-300x158.webp)

### Free digital literacy lessons

Explore lessons at Digital Matters.

## Benefits of Khan Academy

## What to watch out for

Being an educational platform, there is very little risk of exposure to inappropriate or disturbing content while using Khan Academy. Moderation is strict on the community forum. They use AI to quickly remove any comments with bad language.

However, on any platform with community comments there is a chance that something will slip through the cracks, so your child should be prepared to see mean or inappropriate comments if they use the Khan Community forum. You can use our [Digital Resilience toolkit](https://www.internetmatters.org/resources/digital-resilience-toolkit/) to support your child and help them be less effected if they see this kind of content online.

Khan Academy is a US organisation, and therefore its courses are based heavily around the US education system. This can make some lessons, such as the ones based around college admissions, unhelpful for UK children. Explain to your child that this is an American app before they use it. This will help them understand any differences between the American and UK education systems.

Khan Academy can greatly benefit UK children who use it, regardless of their age.

### Description
16,398 views
Posted: 2020-06-03
This video gives a quick overview of how parents can get started with using Khan Academy with their children. It is meant for parents who have kids who are 12 or younger. If you have kids who are 13 or older, please see this video:    • Parent Quick-Start Tips: For Kids Ages 13+  

To start using Khan Academy with your children, visit www.khanacademy.org. 

Get free resources to keep your kids learning during school closures:
https://keeplearning.khanacademy.org/

### Transcript
[0:03] - [Lauren] I'm Lauren from Khan Academy, and today I'm going to give you an overview of how to set up accounts for yourself and your children on Khan Academy.
[0:11] We'll also go over how you can find relevant content for your kids and view their progress.
[0:16] This video is meant for parents with kids who are 12 or under.
[0:20] If you child is 13 or older, please see our other video called Parent Quick Start Tips for Kids Ages 13 Plus.
[0:27] We will start by having your child create an account on Khan Academy.
[0:31] Creating an account lets you and your child track progress and time spent learning.
[0:36] Go to www.khanacademy.org and click Sign up in the upper right-hand corner.
[0:43] On the sign up page, enter your child's date of birth, and click Sign up by choosing a username.
[0:53] On the next page, enter your email address, and choose a username for your child.
[1:10] Then click Sign up. Next, choose a starting point for your child's learning journey.
[1:19] In the Personalize Khan Academy pop-up, select your child's grade and click continue.
[1:26] On the next page, you'll see courses that we recommend for your child. Choose one or more and click continue.
[1:33] You can also click the See all link to view the full menu. Your child is ready to go.
[1:42] Have them click the blue Start button for any course to start with the very first lesson, or click See all to browse the entire course.
[1:51] If you're not sure what level your child is at, here's a tip: Most Khan Academy math courses include a course challenge that can help you quickly find where
[1:59] your child needs practice and where they're already good to go.
[2:03] To get there, scroll to the bottom of the course page and click Start Course challenge.
[2:12] These usually take 30 to 45 minutes and will give you some good clues about where to direct their learning.
[2:18] You can have you child start one grade level below their current grade or even start at kindergarten and work their way up.
[2:26] Next, let's create a parent account.
[2:28] You must create a parent account within seven days, or all child accounts will be deleted. To create an account, check your email.
[2:36] For each child, you'll have an Approve your child's Khan Academy account email waiting.
[2:42] Click the green Allow my child to use Khan Academy button.
[2:46] Check your updates or other mail folders if you don't see this email right away.
[2:52] Follow the prompts to sign up for a new account or sign into an existing account, using the email address where you received the email.
[3:00] Once you sign up, you'll be taken to your parent dashboard.
[3:03] If you want to view your child's progress, you could click on your child's username.
[3:09] This takes you to the progress report, where you can keep track of what they're learning and how much time they're spending.
[3:15] Your child can also see this report through their account by clicking Progress in their left navigation.
[3:20] Thanks for watching, and we hope you and your child enjoy learning on Khan Academy.
